title: Python for DSA
learn: list/dict/set/str ops and their costs, slicing, comprehensions, sorted(key=), collections (deque, Counter, defaultdict), heapq, bisect, float('inf'), tuple unpacking
hook: Interviewers don't care that you know Python. They care that you know what each line costs. `x in my_list` vs `x in my_set` is the difference between O(n²) and O(n).

explain.prompt: An interviewer asks: why would you use a set instead of a list to check whether you've seen a value before? Explain with costs.
keyPoints: list membership (`in`) scans every element: O(n)
set/dict membership hashes the value: O(1) average
inside a loop: list gives O(n²) total, set gives O(n)
trade-off: the set uses O(n) extra memory
